author: Zuhayr Rahman Chowdhury

statements.define: For value-seeking households and small businesses that buy in bulk, Costco offers a paid membership to warehouses of about 4,000 trusted items at the lowest prices.
statements.create: Costco wins on lower cost: markups capped at 14% (15% on Kirkland) and huge volume per item, with a quality kicker from Kirkland. A sustained advantage.
statements.capture: Rivalry and price-sensitive buyers cap grocery margins. Costco keeps more: fees ($5.3B, 92.3% U.S./Canada renewal) are near-pure profit, and volume gives it supplier leverage.
statements.deliver: Limited SKUs, no-frills warehouses, Kirkland and low-turnover staff reinforce each other to keep prices lowest. It refuses wide selection and high merchandise margins.

one_line: Costco trades retail margin for loyalty; watch renewal staying above about 90%.

who: Mid-to-upper-income households buying in bulk, plus small businesses (Business members)
B2C: the member uses, decides and pays; for businesses, the owner decides and pays
what: Hired to stock up on trusted, high-quality goods at the lowest price per unit, in one trip
Today they use supermarkets (Kroger), Walmart, Sam's Club, BJ's, Amazon and Aldi
problem: Supermarkets offer choice at higher prices; discounters are cheap but quality is uneven
Costco closes the gap: curated quality at near-wholesale prices, for an annual fee
define.takeaway: Weakest premise: that members keep renewing for the fee as online sign-ups (which renew less) grow.

wtp_vs_cost: **Moves WTP:** curated quality, Kirkland trust, treasure-hunt items
**Table stakes:** low prices, gas stations, online ordering
**Cost levers:** ~4,000 SKUs, bulk packs, no-frills warehouses
**Wedge:** lower cost: ~11% gross margin vs Walmart's ~24%
map_reading: Axes: quality and trust vs price per unit
Members pick it for quality at near-wholesale prices
Costco on the frontier; Sam's Club inside it
create.takeaway: Low cost with a quality kicker.

vri.resource: Membership model: fees fund low markups
vri.v: Yes: $5.3B fees let prices run near cost
vri.r: Partly: Sam's and BJ's copy the format
vri.i: Hard: 92.3% renewal and scale took decades to build
vri.verdict: Sustained, when paired with the SKU system

vri.v: Yes: huge volume per item lowers unit cost
vri.r: Yes: few retailers commit to ~4,000 SKUs
vri.i: Costly: rivals would lose selection-seeking customers

vri.v: Yes: quality at lower cost; ~25% of sales (est.)

create.vri_takeaway: Each part is copyable alone; the system (fees + few SKUs + Kirkland) is not, because copying it means giving up selection and margin.

forces.logic: Shoppers are fragmented but price-sensitive and switch stores easily; rivals (Walmart, Amazon) and substitutes (Aldi, delivery) raise their power. Keeps grocery markups thin.
forces.firm_power: Yes: the paid fee raises switching costs; renewal 92.3%

forces.logic: Big brands (P&G, Coca-Cola) are concentrated and differentiated; fragmented retailers raise their power, a huge buyer lowers it. Brands keep margin; retailers absorb pressure.
forces.firm_power: Yes: huge volume per SKU and Kirkland as an alternative

forces.logic: Walmart, Sam's, BJ's, Amazon, Kroger, Aldi compete on price; slow growth makes it share-taking.
forces.firm_power: Yes: lowest unit prices plus fee income cushion price wars

forces.logic: Warehouse scale, real estate and supplier terms take decades; online entry is easier but margin-thin.
Online delivery (Amazon, Instacart) and discount grocers (Aldi) replace the bulk trip.
forces.firm_power: Partly: e-commerce and delivery lag Amazon

forces.logic: Credit-card partner (Citi/Visa) and gas add trip value; few complementors take a cut.

capture.takeaway: Rivalry and buyers cap retail margins for everyone; Costco keeps value through fees, not merchandise margin.

deliver.statement: Limited SKUs, membership, Kirkland, no-frills warehouses and well-paid staff form one low-cost system that serves bulk buyers, keeps prices lowest, and locks in members; it refuses wide selection and high markups.
deliver.activities_takeaway: Membership and limited SKUs carry the strategy; Kirkland and staff reinforce them.
reinforcement: Low markups → more members and renewals → fee income → keeps markups low → more volume per SKU → better supplier terms
misaligned: Growing online membership sign-ups renew at lower rates, weakening the renewal engine
judgment: Organized to execute: renewal is the core metric, and turnover is low (about 6 to 8%, est.)
deliver.takeaway: The system depends on one thing: renewal staying above about 90% as fees rise.
